summary: A request from Vint Cerf and Jon Postel at UCLA for a list of the well-known sockets used by network services at each host. They wanted to pick a standard socket for a Discard service and needed to know which were already taken. It notes that socket 1 was the Network Logger used for the Initial Connection Protocol, and asks each site's technical liaison to report their service sockets.

plainLanguage.summary: Before picking a new house number for a new shop, you need to know which numbers are already used. This note asks every computer to list its numbered doors that are already taken.

sections.title: Why a Catalog Is Needed
sections.content: The Network Measurement Group wants to establish a network standard socket number for a Process Discard service. Not all Hosts need to cooperate. To choose a number, the authors must know which sockets at each Host are already allocated to standard network functions.
sections.plainLanguage: They want to open a new service with its own door number, so they first need to know which door numbers are taken.

sections.title: Socket 1 and the Request
sections.content:
At all Hosts that permit login for services, socket 1 is the Network Logger, on which the Initial Connection Protocol (ICP) may be performed.

The authors would like to catalog other sockets that are supposed to be well known. They ask each Host Technical Liaison for a note or phone call describing the function and socket numbers of the network service programs at that Host. The catalog would be published, and they recommend that it be maintained at the NIC.
sections.plainLanguage: Door number 1 is the front desk where you ask to be let in. Everyone is asked to send in a list of their other known doors.

sections.title: What Comes Next
sections.content: The RFC contains no protocol specification. It is a short call for information, with contact details for Vint Cerf and Jon Postel at UCLA, so that Technical Liaisons could respond.
sections.plainLanguage: It is only a letter asking for help, with the writers' phone numbers at the bottom.
